tasks.short: Observe the patient, record vitals, treatment and drugs, write the incident narrative, check the record, send it to the receiving hospital, and hand over to the physician.

steps.what: Paramedic observes the patient's condition and reactions to drugs or treatment
Paramedic records vitals, treatment provided and drugs given on the patient form
Paramedic checks the patient record before handover
Paramedic hands a paper copy of the record to the emergency department
Paramedic reports the patient's condition and treatment to the physician at handover

tasks.design: Vitals from the monitor flow into the electronic patient record on the ambulance tablet ({OTHER}) with time stamps, and drugs and treatments are picked from lists, so the paramedic does not copy numbers onto a form. The narrative uses a short template. Once the paramedic has checked the record, it goes to the receiving hospital's system before arrival. Observing the patient and the verbal handover stay with the paramedic.
tasks.previous_blocker: Vitals and drugs were copied by hand onto a paper form and a copy handed over at the door.
tasks.enabler_now: Ambulance patient records take monitor data and send records to hospitals.
tasks.still_hard: During resuscitation nobody has hands free to record.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a calm patient is getting worse before the monitor shows it.

reach.learn: Whether records arrive before the patient.

evidence.claim: Electronic ambulance patient records can take vital signs from the monitor and send records to hospitals.
Health data are special category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient on scene to the handover; hospital treatment is outside.
Input contract: monitor data by connection to the tablet; drug lists from the ambulance service; fallback is the paper form.
Observing and handover do not change.
The receiving hospital accepts electronic records.
research_questions: Do records arrive complete before the patient?

incremental.description: Paramedic corrects monitor values taken during movement.

approvals.approved_version: The patient record as checked by the paramedic in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short rides with little to record; high: long transports with many vitals and drugs.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Brief the team on interventions on scene, guide them during procedures, prepare training on new protocols, and debrief after difficult calls.

steps.what: Paramedic instructs the emergency medical response team about interventions on scene
Paramedic guides team members during procedures to ensure correct application
Paramedic prepares training on new or changed protocols
Paramedic debriefs the team after difficult calls

tasks.design: Protocol changes come with a summary of what changed and short training slides in the service's document space ({DOCS}), so the paramedic adapts rather than builds training material. Instructing on scene, guiding procedures and debriefing stay with the paramedic.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training on protocol changes was built by each trainer.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared document spaces hold training material per protocol version.
tasks.still_hard: On scene there is no time to look things up.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a young colleague calm during a first resuscitation.

reach.learn: Whether protocol changes are applied sooner.

evidence.claim: Shared document spaces can hold training material per protocol version.

assumptions: Boundary: from the emergency call to the team debriefed; formal accreditation training is outside.
Input contract: protocol changes from the national protocol body; fallback is building training alone.
Instructing, guiding and debriefing do not change.
Team members' time does not change.
research_questions: Are new protocols applied correctly sooner?

incremental.description: Paramedic adds local notes to shared training slides.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few protocol changes; high: a year with many protocol changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Get call details from the dispatch centre, gather history from patient and bystanders, retrieve medication and history, consult the hospital physician, and administer emergency treatment.

steps.what: Paramedic asks the dispatch centre for call details by radio
Paramedic determines the circumstances of the emergency from patient and bystanders
Paramedic obtains the patient's medical history and medication from family or by phone
Paramedic coordinates with treatment center personnel by phone

tasks.design: Call details, address and earlier calls to the same address are pushed from the dispatch system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) to the ambulance tablet, so fewer questions go over the radio. The patient's medication overview and key history can be retrieved on the tablet through the national exchange under emergency access rules, with every look-up logged. Talking with patient and bystanders, consulting the hospital and treating stay with the paramedic.
tasks.previous_blocker: Details came by radio and history from family members and phone calls.
tasks.enabler_now: Dispatch systems push call data to ambulances; health data exchanges allow logged emergency access.
tasks.still_hard: Unknown patients have no record to retrieve.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a frightened relative to tell what really happened.

evidence.claim: Dispatch systems can push call details to ambulance tablets.
Patients may ask who viewed their dossier, so emergency look-ups must be logged.

assumptions: Boundary: from the emergency call to the treatment given; transport is outside.
Input contract: call data from the dispatch centre; history through the national exchange; fallback is radio and phone.
Assessing and treating do not change.
Emergency access follows the exchange's legal rules.
unknowns: Calls with a known patient record.
research_questions: Do paramedics arrive knowing the patient's medication more often?

incremental.description: Paramedic checks retrieved history against what the patient says.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many unknown patients; high: mostly known patients with records.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The paramedic keeps observing, treating, instructing the team and handing over; copying vitals, building training and radio questions shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the electronic patient record on scene
role.ambitious_version: A paramedic with full attention on the patient.
